conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim that prolonged mask use causes dangerous carbon dioxide buildup is false, citing clinical findings, physical properties of gas permeability, and public health consensus. Therefore, it rejects the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup or hypercapnia is **false**.

**Summary of Evidence:**

* **Gas Permeability:** Carbon dioxide and oxygen gas molecules are far smaller than the pores in fabric and surgical mask materials. Consequently, $\text{CO}_2$ freely diffuses through the mask during exhalation rather than accumulating (https://uihc.org/health-topics/do-face-masks-make-you-retain-carbon-dioxide).
* **Occupational Safety:** Occupational health guidelines and medical practice confirm that healthcare personnel safely wear medical masks for extended working hours without compromising oxygenation or retaining dangerous amounts of $\text{CO}_2$ (https://ohsonline.com/articles/2020/08/06/osha-addresses-inaccurate-claims-that-face-coverings-cause-wearer-harm.aspx).
* **Clinical Findings:** Research on gas exchange demonstrates that surgical face masks do not impair breathing, restrict oxygen intake, or elevate blood $\text{CO}_2$ levels—even in vulnerable populations such as patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) (https://www.foxnews.com/health/face-masks-dont-cause-carbon-dioxide-build-up-or-restrict-breathing).
* **Health Official Consensus:** Public health evaluations and medical fact-checks consistently conclude that cloth and surgical masks do not cause hypoxia (oxygen deprivation) or hypercapnia ($\text{CO}_2$ toxicity) (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/).
